map_caption: The map shows the bearings for the meteor. The lighter lines show the directions from the observation sites at the meteor's appearance, and the darker lines show where it was last seen. The blue arrow indicates the visible path of the meteor.
footer_text: This is an automatically generated report from the Norwegian Meteor Network.
df_caption: Dark-flight scenarios for assumed masses and material properties; these do not establish meteorite survival.
df_peak_mag_note: Peak brightness alone does not determine total or surviving mass; a measured light curve and fragmentation constraints are needed.
df_mass_unknown_note: Surviving mass is not constrained. Tracks show hypothetical 5 g–5 kg release masses, not evidence of meteorite survival.
df_sc_hypothetical: Hypothetical fall line (5 g–5 kg at release)
df_mc_assumed_note: Monte Carlo samples fragment masses evenly across the 5 g–5 kg range (logarithmic scale) at the end of luminous flight.
df_mc_no_impacts: No sampled fragments reached the ground, so no MC area is drawn. This does not establish zero surviving mass.
df_frag_3d_unavailable: 3D renderer unavailable. See the current 2D map and statistics.
df_frag_interpretation: Conditional forward sensitivity models, not a fit or survival probability. Mass before the first observed point is not reconstructed. Absolute magnitude refers to distance 100 km, not altitude.
df_frag_inversion_note: First-observed masses were solved independently for each model to reproduce the supplied absolute peak magnitude; they are conditional model inputs, not fitted surviving masses.
df_frag_table_note: Each row is an alternative hypothesis, not an additive mass contribution.
df_frag_unresolved_note: The fate of subgram solids is unresolved; they are not proven to have vaporized or reached the ground.
df_frag_maps_note: Maps show modelled landed cohorts; multiplicities are population weights, not probabilities.
df_frag_no_table_impacts: No modelled ground impacts in these scenarios.
df_frag_warn_generation: Cohort {cohort}: generation cap {limit} reached; continuing intact
df_frag_help_model: Forward fragmentation model represented by this row.
df_frag_help_initial: Mass at the first observed trajectory point; it is an assumed model input, not reconstructed pre-atmospheric mass.
df_frag_help_ablated: Mass removed by ablation during atmospheric flight.
df_frag_help_landed: Explicitly modelled fragment mass predicted to reach the ground.
df_frag_help_unresolved: Mass whose final outcome was not resolved; it is not counted either as vaporized or as landed.
df_frag_help_timeout: Mass still propagating when the model time limit was reached.
df_frag_help_largest: Mass of the largest individual modelled fragment predicted to reach the ground.
df_frag_help_peak_mag: Brightest absolute magnitude predicted by the model at the 100 km reference distance.
df_frag_help_density: Bulk material density assumed for the parent body and fragments.
df_frag_help_lum_eff: Fraction of dissipated kinetic energy converted into luminous radiation.
df_frag_help_shape: Relative weight from range-corrected normalized light-curve shape and post-observed luminous-persistence diagnostics; a relative diagnostic, not a probability that the model is physically true.
df_frag_shape_note: Light-curve shape weights are relative diagnostics, not probabilities that a model is physically true. They include a heuristic penalty for model light predicted after the observed disappearance.
df_frag_help_peak_delay: Predicted peak-light time minus the observed disappearance time; positive means the model peaks after the observations ended.
df_frag_help_post_light: Duration for which the model predicts luminous emission after the observed disappearance.
df_frag_help_preference: Terminal-dominated heuristic preference: shape weight multiplied by exp(-post-observed light / 0.5 s) and an optional normalized density prior, then renormalized. Not a calibrated probability.
df_frag_preference_note: Model preference percentages are terminal-dominated heuristic weights and may include an optional density prior; they are not calibrated physical probabilities.
df_frag_mc_note: Monte Carlo points draw conditional fragment-mass spectra at each model's landed release state; they are what-if realizations, not model probabilities.
df_frag_pref_unavailable: No reliable model preference: the automatic deceleration-derived entry-mass estimate is poorly constrained. Supply --mag or --entry-mass for a conditioned comparison.
df_frag_light_unavailable: Model comparison unavailable: no usable observed camera light curve.
df_frag_warn_inversion: Peak-magnitude mass inversion failed for this experiment; it is shown as unavailable rather than assigned a fallback mass.
